defense_analyst.prose: Atlanta blitzes at a moderate clip: it sends five or more rushers on 25.4% of dropbacks [dc1] over 382 plays [dc2], the 24th-highest rate in the league [dc3], yet its pressure proxy of 17.3% [dc4] ranks 6th best in the league [dc5]. MIN's offense has allowed a pressure proxy of 15.7% [dc6] over 344 plays [dc7], so the protection plan has to handle the extra rusher on passing downs rather than rely on the front alone. Atlanta averages 4.27 pass rushers per dropback [dc8] and has sacked on 5.5% of dropbacks [dc9], so the pocket can break from both the edge and the interior. On the ground, Atlanta puts 6.5 defenders in the box on run plays [dc10], the 23rd-highest count in the league [dc11], and allows success on 44.0% of runs [dc12] with 13.1% of runs going 10 or more yards [dc13]. Run EPA allowed is -0.03 [dc14], so the box holds up on average, but the explosive-run rate is the opening; MIN should attack with gap and zone concepts that create one-on-one lanes, though this data does not split run success by box count. Against the pass, Atlanta allows success on 46.9% of dropbacks [dc15] and 0.08 EPA per pass play [dc16], converts a third-down stop rate of 57.9%, meaning opponents convert 42.1% of third downs [dc17] over 133 plays [dc18], and allows 20-plus-yard pass plays on 8.6% of dropbacks [dc19]. MIN should stay on schedule to keep third-down attempts manageable and be ready to take shots when the pass rush is sending extra bodies.

Punting nets 42.6 yards [kc9] on 38 punts [kc10], with 42.1% [kc11] landing inside the 20, so expect Minnesota to start near midfield. Minnesota averages 28.5 yards [kc16] on 32 kick returns [kc17], so in close games weigh kicking away from its returner. Atlanta's special-teams EPA is -0.04 per play [kc18] on 266 plays [kc19], 26th in the league [kc20], versus 0.13 per play [kc21] for Minnesota on 256 plays [kc22].

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: WR Zachariah Branch is Out [ic1] with a hamstring injury and takes 4.2% [ic2] of team targets over 284 team targets [ic3], a minor shift. DE James Pearce Jr. is Questionable [ic4] with a back injury and has averaged 25.5% of snaps [ic5] over 2 games [ic6]. DT Gervon Dexter Sr. is Questionable [ic7] with an illness and has averaged 57.6% of snaps [ic8] over 10 games [ic9]. Losing either would thin the Atlanta front, so confirm both before kickoff. On the MIN side, WR Jordan Addison is Out [ic10] with a thumb injury and takes 12.7% of team targets [ic11], so those targets shift to the remaining receivers and tight ends. QB Kyler Murray is Out [ic13] with a hamstring injury and carries on 1.7% of team rushes [ic14], so the run game changes less than the passing game. CB Isaiah Rodgers and S Jay Ward are both Questionable, and no MIN front-seven starter is listed.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: The left-side run comes first. Bi.Robinson takes 72.0% of Atlanta's designed rushes [mc1] over 257 designed runs [mc2], and 50.4% of those runs go left [mc3]. Shade the front left and keep a spy on Robinson's cutback, since Atlanta's explosive run rate is 9.7% [mc4]. Atlanta throws on 77.3% of second-and-long plays [mc6] over 88 plays [mc7], so bring pressure and matched coverage there. Atlanta blitzes on 25.4% of dropbacks [mc8] against a MIN pressure proxy of 15.7% [mc9] over 344 plays [mc10], so keep backs and tight ends in protection on passing downs. Opponents convert 42.1% of third downs against Atlanta [mc13] over 133 plays [mc14], so staying on schedule keeps MIN out of obvious passing downs.
